chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a Muslim man who was killed, and his father was a Christian: To whom does his blood money (diyah) belong? He said: 'His blood money is taken and placed in the treasury of the Muslims, because his indemnity/liability is upon the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.بَيْتُ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.دِيَتُهُ: Blood money or compensation for death

ai.seo_question: Who receives the blood money of a Muslim whose father is a non-Muslim?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the blood money of a Muslim whose father is a non-Muslim is paid from the public treasury (*bayt al-mal*) rather than inherited by the father, establishing that the financial liability for the son's life rests with the Muslim community. This ruling underscores the principle of *jina'ah* (blood liability) being communal in this specific context, distinguishing it from standard inheritance laws where the father would typically inherit. It highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the intersection of religious identity and financial obligations within mixed-faith families.
